author: rdc-rfc1-author-b (Claude Haiku 5.5)
rationale: The exported memory-controller reset is a mux of two clk_a reset signals, selected by run_sel_q in the asynchronous clk_b domain. A select change while the inputs differ releases or glitches mc_rst_no at an arbitrary clk_a phase.

author_reading.rationale: The mux select run_sel_q is clocked by clk_b, unrelated to clk_a where both data inputs are launched; when the select changes while the two inputs differ, mc_rst_no can glitch.

labels.rationale: mc_rst_no is a mux whose select run_sel_q is a clk_b flop, while its data comes from clk_a registers. The select can change asynchronously to the clk_a data, so the reset output can glitch.
After boot, clk_b can sample a rising run_i first and select the still-low run reset. clk_a can then make the selected reset high an arbitrarily short interval later.
labels.suspected_flaw: The mux is output-only, so its pulse is outside the async-pin reset-net triggers. The select separately samples a clk_a-timed input on clk_b.

settlement.detection_gap: mc_rst_no is only exported. No local asynchronous reset pin reads it, so the reset mux rules (RDC-009/RDC-017), which start from local reset roots, do not see it. CST-012 (multi-domain output) is outside the RDC deck and does not address the glitch.
settlement.rationale: Both readers are right on bad, critical and class. As B notes, the mux drives only an output, so A's RDC-017/RDC-009 triggers (local reset roots) do not apply, and B's CDC-029/RDC-002/RDC-003 do not target the glitch. The settler records a detection gap and uses A's sites.

was.detection_gap: mc_rst_no is only exported. No local asynchronous reset pin reads it, so the reset mux rules (RDC-009/RDC-017), which start from local reset roots, do not see it. CST-012 (multi-domain output) is outside the RDC deck and does not address the glitch.

adjudication.reason: RDC-009 reports a top-level output that builds a reset from a reset root and a functional leaf (exported reset, consumer outside the design); the frozen detection gap no longer holds
